newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN ELECTRONICS SHARES RETREAT ON YEN AND DOW.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN ELECTRONICS SHARES RETREAT ON YEN AND DOW.

text.p: Shares of leading Japanese high-technology firms retreated on Monday morning in Tokyo, depressed by the higher yen against the dollar and U.S. stocks' tumble on Friday, traders said.

At 0042 GMT, shares of leading computer maker Fujitsu Ltd were down 50 yen at 1,600. Its volume of 1.530 million shares was the fourth-heaviest traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Hitachi Ltd, a leading electronic machinery maker, was down 40 yen at 1,280, with its volume of 1.360 million shares listed as the fifth-heaviest traded issue.

"After stocks fell sharply in New York and the yen surged, sellers led the trading in Tokyo. Especially high-tech issues suffered from profit-taking by foreign investors," said a senior broker at a second-tier Japanese securities house.
Another broker said the share prices were hurt by securities houses' own selling orders.
